headline: A code-generation study reports that structural compliance can conceal incorrect answers
summary: Adikari and Herath evaluated three cost-efficient models across eight combinations of model, coding-agent tool and prompt format on 992 Project Euler problems converted to Java Spring Boot methods. They report near-ceiling compliance with required method signatures and 7,936 executed requests, but only 12.9% of returned answers were correct; 38.4% of generated methods did not compute the value they returned. This is a single-generation, author-reported evaluation on a narrow algorithmic corpus, not a measured rate for enterprise code or deployed assistants.
